text:
Pavel Zacha's name is in the trade columns. The Hockey Writers argued Boston should move him now for the highest value, Causeway Crowd ran an analyst explaining why a deal might be easier than people think, and Daily Faceoff asked what the Bruins should do with him.

He has 14 points in 18 games (5 goals, 9 assists) on 19:14 a night, and his own finishing is right on his chances, 5 goals on 4.7 expected. But Boston has scored 7.9 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and at five on five the Bruins get only 47.2% of the shot attempts with him out there.

There is still plenty to like. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in 60% of the time, exiting his own zone with possession 64% of the time, and in the 86th percentile for chances from in front of the net. His minutes are up two a night over the last ten games.

Our projection has him finishing between 60 and 87 points. What to watch: whether the on-ice scoring holds long enough to matter to a buyer.
